pattern.description: Wind-up of the Zendesk logo assembly: the glyph row (Z half, speech bubble with typing dots, checkmark circle, K half) subtly tightens and reshapes in place, anticipating the collapse into the final mark.
pattern.why_premium: A small anticipatory squeeze before the big morph gives the logo collapse a sense of weight and intention instead of a hard swap; the product icons (chat, resolved check) literally become the brand mark.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline on the four glyph groups: gsap.to(['.zLeft','.bubble','.dots','.checkK'], {x: (i) => inwardOffset[i], scaleX: 0.97, duration: 0.23, ease: 'power2.inOut', stagger: 0}) with the bubble's right edge via a clip-path/width tween; all together, no stagger, as a pre-roll to the e033 collapse.
build_hint.remotion: interpolate(frame, [0, 7], [0, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) driving per-glyph translateX toward centre and a small scaleX on the bubble; no spring (no overshoot visible).

notes: Motion is very subtle across the filmstrip (frames look nearly identical); camera verdict is none, so the 1.11 scale sum is internal content change, likely the glyphs reshaping/tightening. Exact per-glyph direction is uncertain; b01 (union) omitted as redundant with the child boxes.
